subtext.hi: √2, √3, √5 jaise numbers ko fraction (p/q) mein kabhi exactly nahi likha ja sakta — aur ye hum FTA se prove kar sakte hain!
subtext.en: Numbers like √2, √3, √5 can never be written exactly as a fraction (p/q) — and we can prove this using the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic!

text.hi: Irrational numbers ka decimal expansion kabhi khatam nahi hota aur na hi repeat karta hai. Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic ka use karke hum prove kar sakte hain ki √p (p prime ho) hamesha irrational hota hai.
text.en: An irrational number's decimal expansion never ends and never repeats. Using the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, we can prove that √p (where p is prime) is always irrational.

content.hi: Proof by contradiction ka tareeka: pehle assume karo ki √p rational hai (yani p/q form mein likha ja sakta hai, jahan a,b co-prime integers hain aur b≠0).
content.en: Method of proof by contradiction: first assume √p is rational (i.e., can be written as a/b where a, b are co-prime integers and b≠0).

content.hi: Phir dikhao ki ye assumption ek contradiction ki taraf le jaata hai — matlab a aur b dono p ke multiple nikalte hain, jo co-prime hone ke against hai.
content.en: Then show this assumption leads to a contradiction — that both a and b turn out to be multiples of p, which contradicts them being co-prime.

content.hi: Isliye hamara original assumption galat tha — √p irrational hai. Ye method √2, √3, √5, ya kisi bhi prime ke square root ke liye kaam karta hai.
content.en: So our original assumption was wrong — √p is irrational. This method works for √2, √3, √5, or the square root of any prime.

explanation.content: √p ≠ a/b for any co-prime integers a, b (b≠0), when p is prime

steps.hi: Assume √2 = a/b, jahan a,b co-prime hain
steps.en: Assume √2 = a/b, where a,b are co-prime

steps.hi: Isse a² even hai, isliye a bhi even hai (a=2c)
steps.en: So a² is even, hence a is also even (a=2c)

steps.hi: Isse b² bhi even hai, isliye b bhi even hai
steps.en: So b² is also even, hence b is also even

steps.hi: Par a aur b dono even hain — ye co-prime hone ke contradiction hai!
steps.en: But a and b are both even — this contradicts them being co-prime!

steps.hi: Isliye assumption galat tha → √2 irrational hai ✓
steps.en: So the assumption was wrong → √2 is irrational ✓

steps.hi: 3 = a²/b² → a² = 3b² → a² 3 se divisible hai → a bhi 3 se divisible (a=3c)
steps.en: 3 = a²/b² → a² = 3b² → a² is divisible by 3 → a is also divisible by 3 (a=3c)
9c² = 3b² → b² = 3c² → b is also divisible by 3

steps.hi: a aur b dono 3 se divisible — co-prime hone ke contradiction
steps.en: a and b both divisible by 3 — contradicts co-primality

problem.hi: Prove karo ki 5+√3 irrational hai (given √3 irrational hai).
problem.en: Prove that 5+√3 is irrational (given √3 is irrational).

steps.hi: Assume 5+√3 rational hai, kisi rational number r ke barabar
steps.en: Assume 5+√3 is rational, equal to some rational number r

steps.hi: r rational hai, 5 rational hai, isliye r−5 bhi rational hoga
steps.en: r is rational, 5 is rational, so r−5 is also rational

question.hi: √2 irrational hai — ye prove karne ke liye kaunsa method use hota hai?
question.en: Which method is used to prove √2 is irrational?

explanation.hi: Hum √2 ko rational assume karke ek contradiction tak pahunchte hain.
explanation.en: We assume √2 is rational and reach a contradiction.

question.hi: Har irrational number ka decimal expansion terminate ya repeat karta hai.
question.en: Every irrational number's decimal expansion terminates or repeats.

explanation.hi: Galat — irrational numbers ka decimal kabhi terminate ya repeat nahi karta.
explanation.en: False — irrational numbers' decimals never terminate or repeat.

question.hi: Agar p² even hai, to hum p ke baare mein kya keh sakte hain?
question.en: If p² is even, what can we say about p?

explanation.hi: Agar p odd hota, to p² bhi odd hota. Isliye p² even hone ka matlab p bhi even hai.
explanation.en: If p were odd, p² would be odd too. So p² being even means p is also even.

explanation.hi: √5 ek non-perfect-square ka root hai, isliye irrational hai. √4=2, √9=3, √16=4 sab rational hain.
explanation.en: √5 is the root of a non-perfect-square, so it's irrational. √4=2, √9=3, √16=4 are all rational.

notes.hi: Irrational numbers ka decimal kabhi terminate/repeat nahi karta
Proof by contradiction: rational assume karo → contradiction dikhao → isliye irrational
notes.en: Proof by contradiction: assume rational → show contradiction → hence irrational

summary.hi: Proof by contradiction ek powerful tool hai jisse hum kisi bhi √p (p prime) ko irrational prove kar sakte hain.
summary.en: Proof by contradiction is a powerful tool for proving any √p (p prime) is irrational.
